visible_recovery_candidates: P1 textured ear body across four consecutive exact bundle frames; coarse surface plausibly recoverable, fine awns remain below reliable support.
P1 dry strips visible against board, but narrow, low contrast and blurred; broad green-only masks would omit them.
P2 exposed upper curved stem and broad/narrow leaf faces; tangled lower canopy is partly occluded.
P3 exposed lower stem and separated upper leaf faces; reverse leaf faces and hidden junctions unobserved.
P4 upper arch and upright flower stalk track across three nearby exact bundle frames; thin crossing segments and petals are fragile.
P5 green and brown leaf interior controls plus an exposed stem over the pot.
unobservable_or_unresolved: Leaf undersides/back surfaces hidden throughout these predominantly overhead lateral views.
Stem junctions hidden by leaves, soil or pot; no complete base-to-tip path is established.
Fine ear awns, thin petal edges and subpixel dry threads cannot be assumed recoverable from RGB visibility alone.
Some pale leaf crossings lack confirmed specimen attachment; annotations sample visible surfaces, not whole-plant ownership.
comparison_rules: Use the same frozen masks, camera model, pixel raster and occlusion policy for old and new outputs.
Exclude label2 boundaries from primary counts; report their sensitivity separately.
Projected occupancy on foreground RGB pixels is not proof of recovered foreground: a board surface behind a missing stem can project there.

A full-scene cloud correctly contains board geometry. Background-mask occupancy alone is not a false-surface rate; use it to detect plant-mask leakage or independently depth-inconsistent foreground geometry.
No metric depth truth is supplied by these annotations. Report coverage and visual support as proxy evidence, not reconstruction accuracy.
Keep group-level results and visible failure images; do not retune review masks or inflate splats after seeing algorithm output.
